options.text: The movement of particles against a concentration gradient using energy
The movement of water through a partially permeable membrane
The net movement of particles from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration
The movement of large molecules into cells

questions.explanation: Diffusion is the net movement of particles (molecules or ions) from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, down the concentration gradient.

questions.stem: Does diffusion require energy from the cell?

options.text: Only when moving against the gradient
No, it is a passive process

questions.explanation: Diffusion is a passive process that does not require energy from the cell. Particles move due to their own random kinetic energy.

questions.stem: Which factor does NOT affect the rate of diffusion?
questions.explanation: The rate of diffusion is affected by temperature, concentration gradient, surface area, and distance. The colour of the cell has no effect on diffusion.

questions.stem: How does increasing temperature affect the rate of diffusion?

options.text: It increases the rate because particles have more kinetic energy

questions.explanation: Increasing temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, so they move faster and collide more frequently, increasing the rate of diffusion.

options.text: The difference in concentration between two areas
The speed at which particles move

questions.explanation: A concentration gradient is the difference in the concentration of a substance between two regions. Diffusion occurs down the concentration gradient from high to low concentration.

questions.stem: Which substance enters cells by diffusion during respiration?
questions.explanation: Oxygen diffuses into cells from the blood, where it is at a higher concentration, into the cells, where it is used up during respiration and so is at a lower concentration.

questions.stem: Why does a large surface area increase the rate of diffusion?

options.text: It provides more area for particles to cross, allowing more particles to diffuse at once

questions.explanation: A larger surface area provides more space through which particles can move, so more particles can diffuse across at the same time, increasing the overall rate of diffusion.
